items.text: REFERRED TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS
AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO CORPORATIONS, AUTHORITIES AND COMMISSIONS

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the not-for-profit corporation law and the town law, in
relation to the abandonment of cemeteries
items.lawCode: Add §1506-d, amd §1507, N-PC L; amd §291, Town L
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S7835

SPONSOR: RANZENHOFER
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the not-for-profit corporation law and
the town law, in relation to the abandonment of cemeteries

 
PURPOSE:

The bill would create a process through which the state and its locali-
ties are notified of the pending abandonment of state regulated ceme-
teries. This notice allows time to work towards a reorganization of the
cemetery corporation to prevent abandonment, and helps to provide an
orderly transition, if necessary, to municipal control to limit fiscal
impacts on local governments.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new section 1506-d to the Not-for-Profit Corporation
Law outlining cemetery abandonment notification requirements and assist-
ance available to prevent abandonment.

Any state regulated cemetery that is unable to maintain operations and
faces abandonment will be required to provide notice to the State Ceme-
tery Board and the local municipality in which the cemetery is located,
at least 180 days in advance of a potential abandonment.

This notification will trigger State Cemetery Board involvement in an
effort to prevent the abandonment.

In the event that abandonment is not preventable or operations cannot be
transferred to another regulated and solvent cemetery and the condition
of the cemetery operation prevents immediate local takeover of the ceme-
tery, a receiver may be appointed with the consent of the local govern-
ment to manage the cemetery operations until a transfer is possible. Any
costs for such receiverships would come from the already established
state abandoned cemetery fund.

Section 2 amends section 1507(h)(4) of the Not-for-Profit Corporation
Law to allow municipalities and other solvent not-for-profit cemetery
corporations to file an application to the abandoned cemetery fund 25
years after assuming maintenance of abandoned cemeteries for updating
repairs on previously constructed cemetery structures that may need
additional repair.

Section 3 would amend section 291 of the Town Law by adding a new subdi-
vision (5) to limit damages to municipalities for taking over abandoned
cemeteries.

Section 4 states that this bill shall take effect immediately.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

After many years of fiscal stress and the lack of new volunteers, many
financially fragile state regulated cemeteries face abandonment. Under
state law, these abandoned cemeteries become the responsibility of local
municipalities.



Most municipal governments are unprepared or unable to take over these
cemeteries immediately. In many instances, with little or no warning,
local governments find themselves responsible for cemetery operations.

This bill provides for a 180 day process that allows time for efforts to
avoid cemetery abandonment. If efforts to prevent abandonment prove
unsuccessful, it also provides for an orderly transfer of cemetery oper-
ations and access by local governments to the state's abandoned cemetery
fund to pay for costs associated with this transition.

The maintenance and operation of abandoned cemeteries also requires
long-term upkeep and repairs that may not have been discovered at the
time of the abandonment. This legislation allows municipalities or other
qualifying solvent cemeteries that have assumed responsibility for aban-
doned cemeteries to apply for additional funds, 25 years after their
initial application, to assist with repair and maintenance of cemetery
structures existing at the time of the abandonment.

Additionally, since municipalities take over maintenance of abandoned
cemeteries and do not assume title to the property, this bill provides
for protection of the municipality for assuming this control.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act will take effect immediately.
